title: A Scholarship for the Locker
premise: Petra Zhou, a scholarship student who has spent seven years hiding his family's connection to the drowned town beneath Marrowgate Academy, discovers that the school's legendary ghost is leaving him notes in ink that shouldn't exist — notes that know his real name. The ghost is the unclaimed heir of the flooded town, and it can only rest if someone publicly claims its inheritance before the school's centennial gala buries the truth forever. Petra must win both the fencing championship everyone watches and the invisible contest for the school's memory, risking the scholarship, his carefully constructed identity, and his loyalty to the friend whose family helped drown the town. In the end, Petra speaks the ghost's name aloud at the gala, the truth surfaces without destroying him, and he learns that being known is not the same as being erased.
about_author: Rosalind Thornbury is a former archivist who grew up in a river town where half the streets had two names — one on the maps and one in the churchyard. She writes young adult fiction about kids who inherit secrets they never asked for.

chapters.title: The Careful Boy
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Introduce Marrowgate Academy built over the flooded town of Lowmere; establish Petra's seven years of careful invisibility as a scholarship kid with a hidden surname. He memorizes exits, avoids attention, wins nothing on purpose. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Assigned a locker no one has used since the school opened, Petra finds the first note: 'Hello, Petra Zhou' — using the surname he legally buried at age ten. The ink shimmers wrong, like water. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of a careful life.

chapters.title: Rules of the Ghost
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Research montage: the legend of the Lowmere Ghost says it leaves messages only for those it wants something from. His roommate Dev jokes about it; Petra can't laugh. Second note appears: 'You still fence like your grandmother.' Emotional beat: being seen is terrifying.

chapters.title: The Zhou Grip
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, flashback woven in. Fencing tryouts; Coach Voss recognizes the old Lowmere fencing club grip Petra uses unconsciously. Petra deliberately loses the placement bout but is placed on the team anyway. Emotional beat: the past leaking through his body.

chapters.title: Ines Ashford
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Introduce Dev's older sister Ines, student council president and centennial gala chair, charming and ruthless, from the founding Ashford family. She notices Petra noticing things. Emotional beat: a predator's courtesy.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Third note leads him to the sub-basement archive: photographs of Lowmere before the dam, including one of his great-grandmother's fencing team — and an Ashford standing apart from the group. Emotional beat: inheritance as accusation.

chapters.title: Two Championships
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The fencing season begins in earnest while the notes lay out a second, stranger contest: identify what was taken from Lowmere and say it aloud before the gala. Petra realizes the ghost isn't haunting — it's recruiting. Emotional beat: reluctant commitment.

chapters.title: Dev
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev catches Petra sneaking to the archive and covers for him without asking why, revealing his own quiet knowledge that his family's money smells like river mud. Emotional beat: loyalty offered blindly, and how much that costs to accept.

chapters.title: The Ink Test
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Chemistry teacher Ms. Okafor analyzes a note: the ink contains sediment unique to the flooded valley and compounds that oxidize impossibly fast — it should have faded in hours. It hasn't. Emotional beat: wonder cracking open fear.

chapters.title: Ashford House Rules
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines hosts the team dinner; her grandfather's portrait dominates the room. She warns Petra, sweetly, that some scholarships come with conditions and some names are better forgotten. Emotional beat: threat dressed as hospitality.

chapters.title: The Note That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A note addressed to Ines appears in Petra's locker by mistake — or not by mistake. It reads: 'You know what your grandfather took.' Petra must decide whether to give it to her. He does. Emotional beat: choosing honesty as a weapon.

chapters.title: Midterm Losses
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra loses badly at regionals while distracted; Coach Voss confronts him: 'You fence like a boy apologizing for existing.' First honest conversation about why Petra hides. Emotional beat: shame spoken aloud shrinks.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Box
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, home visit. His mother finally opens the box she's kept sealed: the Lowmere fencing club medal, a deed to land under the school, and a letter naming what Elias Ashford took — the town's water rights, then its history. Emotional beat: grief inherited becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Alliance of the Careful
chapters.summary: Dual POV (Petra/Ines). Ines, shaken by the note, approaches Petra with a deal: help her control the story before the gala and she'll protect his scholarship. Both lie. Both know it. Emotional beat: two liars negotiating trust.

chapters.title: The Drowned Gymnasium
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Following the notes' final instruction, Petra and Dev find the sealed flood level of the building: the original Lowmere fencing hall, preserved underwater behind glass, medals still on the wall. One plaque has a blank space where a name was chiseled out. Emotional beat: awe curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: Name Withheld
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The ghost's last note: the chiseled-out name belongs to the true founder of the school's honor code — Petra's great-grandmother, erased so the Ashfords could claim her legacy. Say her name at the gala, or she stays forgotten forever. Emotional beat: the weight of a single sentence.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Ines gives Dev an ultimatum: report Petra's archive break-ins or lose his position and references. Dev burns the evidence instead. Emotional beat: loyalty defined not as silence but as choice.

chapters.title: Semifinals
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra fences the tournament of his life, no longer hiding the Zhou grip, winning openly in front of the whole school. Ines watches from the stands, recalculating. Emotional beat: visibility as victory.

chapters.title: The Gala Begins
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Centennial night: chandeliers, donors, Ines's flawless speech crediting her grandfather with everything. Petra holds the medal in his pocket. The blank plaque gleams behind glass in the display hall. Emotional beat: held breath.

chapters.title: The Name
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Climax. Petra takes the stage during the dedication, and before the whole school says his great-grandmother's name — Mei-Lin Zhou — and what the Ashfords took. The lights fail; every glass case fogs with river breath; the ink of the gala program runs like water. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into release.

chapters.title: After the Water Recedes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Fallout: the board investigates, Ines chooses to confirm the record rather than fight it, the plaque is recut. The ghost leaves one final note in ordinary fading ink: 'Thank you, Petra.' Then nothing. Emotional beat: quiet after a long storm.

chapters.title: A Scholarship for the Locker
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Epilogue. Petra keeps locker 114, now officially his, and leaves a note inside for whoever needs it next: 'You're allowed to be known.' He fences the final wearing his full name on his jacket. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed as identity, freely chosen.
